entries.subjective_report: Saturday Kiara ride focused on Stumpjumper clipless cleat position and 2K+ trail transfer. Clayton moved cleat position back and forth between laps, with longer rest before climbing back to 2K while testing changes. Most laps were 2K+ because it has more roots, roughness, and a punchy climb, giving a better gauge of overall riding. When the cleat position felt correct, it felt natural and allowed full use of the Stumpjumper 140 mm fork travel.
entries.coaching_interpretation: Treat this as a controlled equipment-rider interaction note: improved cleat position likely improved foot security, dynamic centering, front tyre authority, and bike-body separation. Do not over-credit the cleat alone; validate by repeat 2K+/2K performance, braking timing, line choice, and whether full fork travel occurs without harshness, pitching, or sloppy timing.
review_questions: Did correct cleat position improve corner entry and exit timing, or mainly comfort?
Did full fork travel come from better loading and speed, or from overdriving/harsh impacts?
Did the final 2K+ lap preserve braking timing and line choice compared with the first clean lap?
